 Project Story 

 About the Project 

 StockPilot is an AI-powered trading research terminal that helps users explore markets, analyze stocks, review SEC filings, compare technical charts, and manage a virtual portfolio. 

 It combines real market data with WebMCP tools, allowing an AI agent to interact directly with the application. Users can ask the agent to research a ticker, open stock pages, analyze filings, draw chart patterns, screen stocks, and simulate trades. 

 Inspiration 

 We wanted to make financial research more interactive and accessible. Traditional market tools often require users to navigate through many separate screens, interpret complex charts, and manually connect information from news, filings, financial data, and portfolio performance. 

 StockPilot was inspired by the idea of an AI assistant that does more than answer questions. It should be able to take meaningful actions inside the trading terminal, such as opening an analysis page, highlighting important SEC passages, configuring a comparison chart, or creating a simulated position. 

 How We Built It 

 StockPilot was built with: 

 
 Next.js and React for the application interface 
 TypeScript for type-safe application logic 
 Finnhub for quotes, company profiles, news, recommendations, financials, earnings, and SEC filing metadata 
 Supabase for persisted market data and application storage 
 WebMCP for exposing StockPilot actions to compatible AI agents 
 Local OHLCV datasets for historical charting, indicators, pattern detection, and backtesting 
 Tailwind CSS and reusable UI components for the trading terminal interface 
 

 The application includes tools for: 

 
 Stock search and detailed quote lookup 
 Market news and sector performance 
 Stock screening and ranking 
 SEC filing review and risk analysis 
 Technical pattern detection 
 Support and resistance calculations 
 Portfolio analysis and risk scoring 
 Virtual buying and selling 
 Price alerts and watchlists 
 Strategy backtesting 
 Multi-stock chart comparison and technical drawings 
 

 Challenges We Ran Into 

 One major challenge was coordinating AI actions with a client-side application. Fetching data is straightforward, but actions such as navigation, chart updates, and filing highlights must be synchronized with the correct page and component state. 

 We also had to handle incomplete or unavailable provider data. SEC filings may not always include a readable report URL, and free-tier APIs can return limited results. To keep the experience reliable, StockPilot uses fallbacks, validation, normalized filing content, and best-effort analysis. 

 Another challenge was making technical chart interactions precise. Drawing points need to align with real trading dates and meaningful price ranges, so the application snaps dates to available candles and clamps prices to valid OHLCV boundaries. 

 Accomplishments We’re Proud Of 

 We are proud that StockPilot is more than a dashboard. It is an interactive environment where an AI agent can: 

 
 Navigate users to relevant pages 
 Retrieve and summarize real market data 
 Analyze SEC filings and calculate risk signals 
 Highlight important filing passages 
 Configure chart styles, indicators, and time ranges 
 Detect and draw technical patterns 
 Compare multiple companies 
 Simulate portfolio actions while enforcing authentication boundaries 
 

 The WebMCP integration gives the AI a practical interface to the product instead of limiting it to text-only responses. 

 What We Learned 

 We learned that building an AI-enabled application requires designing both the user interface and the action interface at the same time. Tool descriptions, input schemas, validation, navigation behavior, and error messages are all part of the user experience. 

 We also learned the importance of grounding financial analysis in concrete data. Historical prices, filing documents, recommendation trends, and portfolio state should be traceable to actual application data rather than invented assumptions. 

 Finally, we learned that asynchronous workflows need careful handling. Data fetching, page navigation, event dispatching, and component mounting must work together so that an AI-triggered action remains understandable and reliable to the user. 

 What’s Next for StockPilot 

 Next, we plan to improve StockPilot with: 

 
 More reliable cross-page AI action handoffs 
 Expanded market and sector coverage 
 More advanced portfolio analytics 
 Additional technical indicators and drawing tools 
 Richer SEC filing comparisons across reporting periods 
 Persistent user portfolios and watchlists through Supabase 
 More robust authentication and account management 
 Improved backtesting with transaction costs and risk controls 
 Broader WebMCP support for agent-driven financial workflows 
 

 Our long-term goal is to make StockPilot a trustworthy collaborative workspace where people and AI agents can research markets together while keeping decisions transparent, data-grounded, and user-controlled.
